title: Type Safety in CuTe DSL
critical_patterns: Always annotate kernel parameters for type safety
Use specific scalar types like cutlass.Int32 instead of Python int
Explicit casts are preferred for type conversions
constraints: All kernel parameters must have type annotations
Types are checked at compile time
Missing type annotations cause compile errors
Implicit conversions may lead to precision loss
Constexpr values must be known at compile time
compressed_summary: CuTe DSL emphasizes type safety through mandatory type annotations for kernel parameters, enabling compile-time type checking and optimization. This strong typing paradigm helps catch errors early, improving performance and clarity. Key types include cute.Tensor for generic tensors and various cutlass scalar types for integers and floats. Type inference is supported for local variables and return types, but explicit annotations are required for parameters. Compile-time constants are handled using cutlass.Constexpr, ensuring values are known during compilation. Common errors include missing type annotations, type mismatches, and incorrect use of Constexpr. Best practices involve always annotating parameters, using specific types instead of generic Python types, and preferring explicit casts for conversions. These practices lead to earlier error detection, better performance, and self-documenting code, with enhanced IDE support. CuTe DSL's type system also supports runtime type validation and specialization based on tensor dtypes, allowing for efficient and safe GPU kernel execution.
